original_question: Let C_1 and C_2 be compact convex sets in a Hilbert space H. Must there exist a point x in H such that, if p_i is a projection of x onto C_i for i in {1,2}, then the normal vector x - p_i defines a supporting hyperplane that strongly exposes the singleton face {p_i} of C_i? Here a point p in a convex set C is strongly exposed by a linear functional f when f(p) = sup_{x in C} f(x) and every sequence (x_k) in C with f(x_k) approaching sup_{x in C} f(x) converges to p.
target_in_paper: The unnamed conjecture in Section 5, "Projections onto Compact Convex Sets" (problem proposed by Andrew Eberhard), previewed in the Introduction as the Section 5 question about finding a point whose projections are singleton faces strongly exposed by the relevant normals. ([espace.curtin.edu.au](https://espace.curtin.edu.au/bitstream/handle/20.500.11937/81338/81402.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper very closely: it has the right ambient setting (two compact convex sets in a Hilbert space), the correct existential quantifier over a point x in H, the use of the projections p_i onto C_i for i=1,2, the role of the normals x-p_i, and the requirement that these normals define hyperplanes strongly exposing the singleton faces {p_i}. It also reproduces the paper’s recalled definition of strong exposure via convergence of maximizing sequences. ([espace.curtin.edu.au](https://espace.curtin.edu.au/bitstream/handle/20.500.11937/81338/81402.pdf))
missing_details: The paper presents this as a conjecture/open problem in Section 5, not as an established theorem. ([espace.curtin.edu.au](https://espace.curtin.edu.au/bitstream/handle/20.500.11937/81338/81402.pdf))

To make the question fully stand-alone, p_i should be written explicitly as the metric projection p_i := P_{C_i}(x), rather than left as a conditional "if p_i is a projection." The nearby context uses the projection-operator notation P_{C_i}(x). ([espace.curtin.edu.au](https://espace.curtin.edu.au/bitstream/handle/20.500.11937/81338/81402.pdf))

It is better to state that C_1 and C_2 are nonempty compact convex sets, since otherwise the projections P_{C_i}(x) are not defined. The paper omits "nonempty," but that assumption is needed in a stand-alone formulation. ([espace.curtin.edu.au](https://espace.curtin.edu.au/bitstream/handle/20.500.11937/81338/81402.pdf))

The paper recalls strong exposure in terms of a continuous linear functional, so the normal x-p_i should be translated into the functional y ↦ ⟨x-p_i, y⟩ (or, equivalently, the supporting hyperplane orthogonal to x-p_i through p_i). ([espace.curtin.edu.au](https://espace.curtin.edu.au/bitstream/handle/20.500.11937/81338/81402.pdf))

The Section 5 context says this conjecture arises from a special case of Chebyshev’s conjecture, namely the question whether there exists x with P_{C_1}(x)=P_{C_2}(x); that motivation is paper-faithful context, but it is not itself part of the conjecture. ([espace.curtin.edu.au](https://espace.curtin.edu.au/bitstream/handle/20.500.11937/81338/81402.pdf))
refined_question: Let C_1 and C_2 be nonempty compact convex subsets of a Hilbert space H. Does there always exist a point x ∈ H such that, for each i ∈ {1,2}, if p_i := P_{C_i}(x) denotes the metric projection of x onto C_i, then the continuous linear functional y ↦ ⟨x-p_i, y⟩ strongly exposes p_i in C_i; equivalently, the supporting hyperplane {y ∈ H : ⟨x-p_i, y⟩ = ⟨x-p_i, p_i⟩} strongly exposes the singleton face {p_i} of C_i? In other words, must there exist x ∈ H such that for i=1,2 one has ⟨x-p_i, p_i⟩ = sup_{y∈C_i}⟨x-p_i, y⟩ and every sequence (y_k) in C_i satisfying ⟨x-p_i, y_k⟩ → sup_{y∈C_i}⟨x-p_i, y⟩ converges to p_i? ([espace.curtin.edu.au](https://espace.curtin.edu.au/bitstream/handle/20.500.11937/81338/81402.pdf))
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 5 rather than any other problem in the paper. The Introduction summarizes Section 5 using essentially the same language about projections onto compact sets in a Hilbert space and singleton faces strongly exposed by the relevant normals, and Section 5 then states the conjecture almost verbatim for compact convex sets C_1 and C_2. The only real refinements needed are editorial: make the projection notation explicit as P_{C_i}(x), align the exposure clause with the paper’s recalled definition via continuous linear functionals, and add nonemptiness so the question is fully stand-alone. The sentence about P_{C_1}(x)=P_{C_2}(x) is included by the paper as motivation from Chebyshev-set theory, not as an equivalent reformulation of the conjecture. ([espace.curtin.edu.au](https://espace.curtin.edu.au/bitstream/handle/20.500.11937/81338/81402.pdf))
